title_en: From a Scratch to a World Without Smallpox
title_zh: 从一道划痕到天花绝迹
english_paragraphs: Smallpox, a contagious affliction, killed about three in ten of its sufferers and an estimated 300 million in the 20th century. An early safeguard, deliberately implanting matter from its sores in the healthy, was practised in China by the 16th century and reached England in 1721. The procedure itself could cause grave sickness or death, if less frequently than natural smallpox.

Rustic lore held that milkmaids with cowpox, a mild ailment of livestock, were immune to smallpox. In 1774 Benjamin Jesty, a Dorset farmer, employed cowpox to protect his wife and two sons. On 14 May 1796 Edward Jenner, a provincial practitioner, inserted fluid from a milkmaid's cowpox sore into a scratch on eight-year-old James Phipps.

On 1 July 1796 Jenner exposed the boy to smallpox; no symptoms ensued. In 1797 the Royal Society declined to publish his paper, judging his evidence unconvincing. In June 1798 he privately funded his book, the Inquiry, with supplementary cases. The word vaccine derives from the Latin vacca, cow.

Jenner was not the idea's originator. His contribution was a test, with results accessible in print, so other doctors could replicate and disseminate the technique. By today's standards, experimentation on a child without informed consent would be unethical. Jenner died on 26 January 1823, with smallpox far from eliminated.

In 1967 the WHO launched an intensified, concerted campaign to eradicate smallpox. The last naturally occurring case was diagnosed in Somalia on 26 October 1977. On 8 May 1980 the World Health Assembly formally declared the world free of smallpox, the only human disease ever wiped out. That pronouncement came almost 184 years after Phipps was vaccinated.
chinese_source_paragraphs: **天花**(Smallpox)，一种**传染性的**(contagious)**疾病**(affliction)，夺去了约三成**患者**(sufferers)的生命，并且估计有3亿人在20世纪丧命。一种早期的**防护手段**(safeguard)，是**有意**(deliberately)把天花**脓疮**(sores)中的**物质**(matter)**植入**(implanting)健康人体内，到16世纪，中国已在**施行**(practised)这种方法，1721年又传入英国。这种**做法**(procedure)本身可能导致**严重的**(grave)**疾病**(sickness)或死亡，尽管不如自然天花那样**频繁**(frequently)。

**乡间**(Rustic)**传说**(lore)认为，挤奶女工若得过牛痘这种**牲畜**(livestock)的**轻微**(mild)**病症**(ailment)，
{{（一般指牛的牛痘，轻微病症）|ailment}}就**对**(immune to)天花**免疫**(immune to)。1774年，本杰明·杰斯蒂，一位多塞特郡农夫，**使用**(employed)牛痘来保护他的妻子和两个儿子。1796年5月14日，爱德华·詹纳，一位**地方**(provincial)**执业医师**(practitioner)，将取自一名挤奶女工牛痘疮的**液体**(fluid)，**注入**(inserted)8岁的詹姆斯·菲普斯的一道**划痕**(scratch)中。

1796年7月1日，詹纳**让**(exposed to)这个男孩**接触**(exposed to)天花；任何**症状**(symptoms)都没有**随之出现**(ensued)。1797年，皇家学会拒绝去**发表**(publish)他的论文，认为他的证据**缺乏说服力**(unconvincing)。1798年6月，他**私人**(privately)**出资**(funded)出版了他的著作《探究》，书中附上了**补充**(supplementary)病例。表示**疫苗**(vaccine)的英文词**源自**(derives from)**拉丁语**(Latin)的vacca，意思是牛。

詹纳并不是这一想法的**首创者**(originator)。他的贡献是一项试验，其结果在已出版的书籍中**可以获得**(accessible)，以便其他医生能够**复制**(replicate)并**传播**(disseminate)这项**技术**(technique)。按今天的标准，拿孩子做**实验**(experimentation)在没有取得**知情**(informed)**同意**(consent)的情况下，属于**不道德**(unethical)行为。詹纳于1823年1月26日去世，那时天花还远未被**消除**(eliminated)。

1967年，世界卫生组织发起了一场**强化**(intensified)、**共同筹划的**(concerted)运动，要**根除**(eradicate)天花。最后一例**自然**(naturally)**发生**(occurring)的病例于1977年10月26日在索马里**确诊**(diagnosed)。1980年5月8日，世界卫生大会**正式**(formally)宣布全世界已摆脱天花，天花也成为迄今唯一被**彻底消灭**(wiped out)的人类疾病。那一**宣告**(pronouncement)，出现在菲普斯**接种疫苗**(vaccinated)之后的近184年。

sentences.english: On 8 May 1980 the World Health Assembly formally declared the world free of smallpox, the only human disease ever wiped out.
sentences.chinese_source: 1980年5月8日，世界卫生大会**正式**(formally)宣布全世界已摆脱天花，天花也成为迄今唯一被**彻底消灭**(wiped out)的人类疾病。

sentences.english: That pronouncement came almost 184 years after Phipps was vaccinated.
sentences.chinese_source: 那一**宣告**(pronouncement)，出现在菲普斯**接种疫苗**(vaccinated)之后的近184年。

approved_summary: 天花约致三成患者死亡；早期人痘术把天花疮中物质接种给健康人作预防，风险虽低于自然染病，仍可能致重病或死亡。
乡间传牛痘可防天花；农夫杰斯蒂1774年已用牛痘保护家人，詹纳并非首创。
詹纳1796年给男孩种牛痘，再让他接触天花而未发病；无知情同意的儿童试验按今天标准不合伦理。
皇家学会嫌证据不足拒稿后，詹纳自费公布试验和补充病例，使其他医生能够重复验证、传播技术。
世卫1967年强化行动，1977年出现最后自然病例；1980年世界卫生大会宣布根除天花，迄今唯一被根除的人类疾病。
